key_insight: Pressure can be treated as a geometric potential that curves an effective space, linking fluid motion, vortex criteria, and pressure Poisson constraints through a single geometric framework.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified way to interpret and potentially classify vortical structures in turbulence, especially for comparing Eulerian and Lagrangian detection methods.
method: Build a Newton–Cartan geometric description of the flow
Apply a conformal transformation to the spatial metric so pressure appears as curvature
Relate vortex-identification criteria to geometric invariants/projections of the effective curvature
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation and consistency argument, showing recovery of the Euler equation in the weak-field limit and deriving the pressure Poisson equation from geodesic and Bianchi identities.
watch_item: The framework is primarily analytical and geometric, so practical vortex detection would still require careful numerical discretization and validation on real turbulent data.
paper_title: On the relationships between pressure geometrization and vortex identification
